title.narrative: UNDP Strategic Partnership for Resilience, Governance, and Development 2025–2027

description.narrative:
The agreement establishes a joint strategic partnership between UNDP/PAPP and the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs for the period July 2025 to December 2027, with a total commitment of NOK 300 million. This agreement consolidates five existing project-based specific agreements into a single consolidated agreement to enhance strategic coherence, operational efficiency, and development impact in Palestine. One of its defining features is the inclusion of an unallocated commitment, which provides programmatic flexibility. This mechanism enables timely adaptation to shifting political dynamics and humanitarian challenges. It also allows for the initiation of new activities in response to emerging needs, ensuring the agreement remains relevant and responsive in a rapidly evolving context.
This program is designed to address both the early recovery needs, as well as the deeper, structural development of institutions. At its core, the agreement aims to streamline administrative processes by introducing a unified grant framework, making implementation more efficient and coherent. It will deliver rapid, life-preserving interventions for vulnerable groups. Activities include Cash-for-Work programs, emergency health and education services, WASH support, and rubble removal in Gaza. Education continuity is prioritized through safe learning environments and emergency support for schools in Gaza and vulnerable West Bank communities. Focuses on restoring livelihoods and public service systems. Includes job creation, SME support, rehabilitation of damaged infrastructure, school rehabilitation, and solar energy solutions for essential services. In East Jerusalem, recovery efforts strengthen education access by rehabilitating schools, improving learning conditions, and expanding community engagement initiatives.
